blocks.text: 1. Hybrid Search
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447304276-116800745.png
Hybrid search combines semantic and keyword search into one system, resolving the tradeoff between the two by refusing to pick just one.
It runs both retrieval methods together and merges their results into one ranking.
2. Applying Hybrid Embeddings To Retrieval
Hybrid embeddings already combined dense and sparse scores at the vector level.
Hybrid search applies that same combining idea to the full retrieval pipeline.
3. Two Retrieval Methods, Two Strengths
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447304276-194571332.png
Semantic search brings conceptual understanding and keyword search brings exact match precision, each method winning where the other struggles.
Combining both means fewer queries fall through the gap between them.

blocks.text: 4. Running Both Retrieval Pipelines
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447304276-597438896.png
A hybrid system sends the same query to both a semantic search index and a keyword search index.
Each pipeline returns its own independently ranked list of candidate chunks.
5. Merging Scores Across Different Scales
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447304276-986223380.png
Hybrid embeddings already combined two scores into one; here, a semantic similarity score and a BM25 score live on completely different numeric scales.
A combination formula has to reconcile those two very different measurements.
6. Reciprocal Rank Fusion In Retrieval
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447304277-218175688.png
Reciprocal rank fusion, introduced with hybrid embeddings, combines results based on each one's rank position, sidestepping the scale mismatch entirely.
A chunk ranked highly by either method rises toward the top of the merged results.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A chunk ranked first by keyword search but tenth by semantic search still rises near the top of the merged results under reciprocal rank fusion, since its strong showing in either method counts.

blocks.text: 7. Weighting Semantic Versus Keyword Signal
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447304277-452677932.png
Adjusting how much weight semantic results versus keyword results carry shifts the final ranking.
Different applications benefit from leaning more one direction or the other.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A technical support system handling many exact error codes benefits from weighting keyword results more heavily, while a general question answering assistant leans more toward semantic results.

blocks.text: 8. Added Infrastructure Cost
Hybrid embeddings already touched on the added complexity and cost; maintaining both a semantic index and a keyword index doubles the moving pieces.
That real engineering cost has to be weighed against the retrieval quality gained.

blocks.content: {"headers":["System type","Infrastructure to maintain"],"rows":[["Single method","One index"],["Hybrid search","Two indexes plus a fusion step"]]}

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Hybrid Search Is Worth The Added Complexity

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Hybrid Search Is Worth The Added Complexity
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447304277-564240197.png
Production systems facing varied, unpredictable queries benefit most from hybrid search.
Narrow, predictable query patterns, by contrast, may not need the extra complexity of running both methods.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Comparing raw semantic and keyword scores directly without a proper fusion method.
Using equal weighting for both methods without testing whether a domain benefits from leaning either way.
Underestimating the infrastructure cost of maintaining two separate retrieval indexes.
Assuming hybrid search is always better without measuring actual retrieval quality gains.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Hybrid search runs both semantic and keyword retrieval together and merges their results.
It applies the same combining idea from hybrid embeddings to the full retrieval pipeline.
Semantic and keyword search each win where the other struggles, covering each other's gaps.
A hybrid system sends the same query to both a semantic index and a keyword index.
Semantic and keyword scores live on different scales, requiring a combination formula.
Reciprocal rank fusion combines results by rank position, sidestepping the scale mismatch.
Weighting semantic versus keyword signal lets a system lean toward the strength its domain needs.
Maintaining two indexes adds real infrastructure cost that must be weighed against quality gains.
